newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE confirms will send mission to Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: OSCE confirms will send mission to Yugoslavia.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed on Tuesday it would send a delegation to Belgrade in the next few days to investigate a disputed local election last month.
In a statement, the OSCE said the mission would be headed by former Spanish Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez. "The delegation is expected to leave for Belgrade in the coming days," it said.

Europe's top security body said the decision to send a team to Belgrade followed an invitation extended last week by Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to Flavio Cotti, the OSCE's current Chairman-in-Office.

"Mr. Cotti has asked the Special Representative to seek information from all political forces and institutions, including the media, and from the judiciary on the facts and events relating to the municipal elections, including the annulment of their results," the statement said.

The reversal of an originally reported opposition victory in the polls has caused an unprecedented four-week campaign of mass protests against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on the streets of Belgrade and other large Serbian cities.

"Mr. Cotti expects that the Special Representative will enjoy free access to all the persons, insitutions, election commissions and documents that he considers necessary," the OSCE said, adding Gonzalez would subsequently offer any recommendations he deemed necessary.
